extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers and journalism professionals interested in wartime reporting and press policy
extracted.subtask_description: Contemporary newspaper coverage and commentary on wartime events, press freedom, and the role/quality of foreign correspondents. Includes dispatches, casualty lists, shipyard/launch reports and editorials about the press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free press / unrestricted news flow
rubrics_metrics.description: News should be permitted to flow unhampered between nations; where that flow is dammed up it becomes a new danger spot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorials and commentators urge fostering a 'crusade' for a free press so people of all countries may enjoy the constitutional right to information; suppression (as under Hitler) is singled out as a root of danger and conquest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and impartiality in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting must be accurate and impartial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes 'accurate and impartial reporting' as essential to good foreign correspondence and to prevent misinformation or manipulation; cited historically against press control by totalitarian regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-caliber foreign correspondents / truth-finding
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign correspondents must be of the highest type, equipped to find where the truth lies and to 'paint in the background' for readers in the complex postwar world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondents will face the largest assignment of the generation: locating truth in shattered societies, providing context/background, and serving readers; the quality of correspondents will determine the service newspapers and agencies can render.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational independence of news agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: News agencies should be structured to guarantee independence and prevent control by any single interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Reuters' reorganization and the creation of a Reuters Trust (foundation) to guarantee the agency could not pass into the hands of any one particular interest; ownership equality among constituent press groups is presented as a safeguard of integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain press quality despite resource constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should sustain vigorous reporting and editorial quality even when size/page counts are reduced by wartime shortages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations from Australia: despite cuts in size due to shortages, newspapers were judged to be doing an 'extraordinarily good job'—implying resource limits should not justify lowering reporting standards.
